title: Lemonade Change
summary: At a lemonade stand, each lemonade costs $5.
statement: At a lemonade stand, each lemonade costs $5. Customers pay with $5, $10, or $20 bills. You start with no change. Given an array of bills, determine if you can always give the correct change so each customer pays exactly $5.
constraints: Each lemonade costs five and customers pay 5, 10, or 20 in order.
Start with no change and return whether exact change can be given to everyone.
hints: For a twenty, spending one ten preserves more five-dollar bills than spending three fives.
Track counts of fives and tens, greedily prefer 10+5 for fifteen change.
On 10 spend one five; on 20 spend 10+5 else three fives; reject shortages.
Tens have no use except twenty-dollar change, while fives are required for both, so preserving fives is optimal.
editorial: Tens have no use except twenty-dollar change, while fives are required for both, so preserving fives is optimal.

tests.explanation: Three fives cover the ten-dollar and then the twenty-dollar change.
After two ten-dollar customers, no five remains for the final twenty.
